question_text: The President of the United States can serve only two terms. Why?
lead_in: Either of these works (you only need one):

official_answers.text: To keep the president from becoming too powerful

why_it_matters.text: Two terms is enough time for a president to govern, but not so long that they become a permanent ruler. The limit is a deliberate guardrail against the kind of one-person power the colonists rebelled against. It keeps the presidency — even with all its power — temporary, accountable, and democratic.

fun_fact.text: George Washington could have ruled for life — but chose to step down after 8 years. His example held for 144 years. Then Franklin D. Roosevelt broke it, winning 4 terms during the Depression and WWII. After he died in office, Congress proposed the 22nd Amendment to lock in the two-term limit. Ratified 1951.
